clue.text: Operations unit making huge bomb

parts.note: mega- is a prefix meaning huge, as in megastar
a show that bombs is a flop, a failure

explanation.surface: A bomb disposal unit is busy with an enormous explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operations unit' suggests a military team handling the bomb, but it is the definition: a computing measure of a million floating-point operations per second.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing this is a measure of processing speed, a million floating-point calculations every second.

clue.text: Canines watch over force

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting over another is placed above it, so it comes first

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
teeth are the force or power behind a rule, as in a law with teeth

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on the dogs when force is used.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the pointed canine teeth of the upper jaw, so named because they lie under the eyes.

clue.text: Delivery of salt by helicopter?

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, and delivering him from danger by helicopter over the water is a rescue mission

explanation.surface: Bags of table salt are being dropped by helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' is crossword shorthand for a seasoned sailor, and 'delivery' means saving rather than dropping off goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt is a sailor, and saving one from the waves by helicopter is exactly a coastguard mission of this kind.

clue.text: Sharp-sighted broadcaster's to join team

indicators.note: a broadcaster's version of something is how it sounds when spoken on air

parts.note: to join is to link, and a team is a side, giving link side

explanation.surface: A keen-eyed radio presenter is signing up to play for a team.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'link side' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx was proverbially credited with exceptional vision, so having its eyes means seeing very keenly.

clue.text: French singer ate and jogged on the spot

parts.note: Edith Piaf was the celebrated French chanteuse
someone who ate has fed

explanation.surface: Edith Piaf had a meal and then went running without moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: To piaffe is a dressage term: a horse trots in place without advancing.
explanation.definitionFit: In dressage, the piaffe is a trot performed in place, the horse lifting its legs without moving forward.

clue.text: University dons' hearts broken, missing Oxford perhaps

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive apostrophe adding no letter
H is the card-game abbreviation for the suit of hearts

explanation.surface: Academics at a university are heartbroken and one of them is missing Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university, but here it is a laced leather shoe; 'broken' is the signal to rearrange the dons and hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a type of laced shoe, so a person lacking one is without footwear.

clue.text: Surfers click with these shy people

definitions.meaning: web surfers point and click with a computer pointing device
timid people are often likened to small rodents, as in 'quiet as a ...'

explanation.surface: Surfers and shy people are lumped together.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer users point with these desktop devices, and timid, retiring people are called by the same rodent name.

clue.text: Note on alcoholic chap just seen by specialist

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes
a sot is a habitual drunkard
Eric is a typical man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A doctor's note about a heavy-drinking man who has just been to see a consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a doctor's letter, but it is just the musical note E.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small circle of initiates or experts.

clue.text: After struggle, gain return fit for a saint

indicators.note: the word that comes after struggle is twisted about, so its letters are rearranged
to return is to go back, so the word for fit is read backwards

parts.note: to fit someone is to suit them

explanation.surface: Someone recovers from a struggle and is fit enough to be a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After struggle' reads as a time phrase, but it tells you to scramble the word that follows; 'return' turns the synonym for fit backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignatius of Loyola, founder of the Jesuits, is one of several canonised holy men bearing this name.

clue.text: Boo fool losing way

indicators.note: losing means the letters for way are taken out of the word for fool

parts.note: a jester was a court fool
ST, for street, is a common abbreviation standing for a way

explanation.surface: Someone boos a fool who has lost their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes ST out of JESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To boo is to mock or shout derision at someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Corporal punishment used in Thebes?

definitions.meaning: a traditional caning of half a dozen strokes
the city name Thebes is spelt with six letters taken from the phrase 'the best'

explanation.surface: A question about whether caning was practised in ancient Thebes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful one: THEBES uses six of the seven letters of THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A caning of half a dozen strokes was the classic school beating, and Thebes is spelt from six letters of the phrase.

clue.text: Monster takes branches and top of tree apart

indicators.note: taken apart means broken into pieces and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged
the top of a word in an across or down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monster rips branches and the crown of a tree to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is BRANCHES, AND and T, the first letter of 'tree', scrambled together.
explanation.definitionFit: This frumious creature comes from Lewis Carroll's nonsense poems, a fearsome beast to be shunned.

clue.text: Study light: get one out of ten

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom

indicators.note: taking a letter out means removing it from the word for light

parts.note: an airy room is light and bright
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: In a well-lit study, someone scores just one out of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one out of ten' reads like a poor mark, but 'one out' deletes I from AIRY, leaving 'of ten' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A denary system counts in tens, as in decimal notation.

clue.text: Risk death with nettle

parts.note: death is the end of life
to nettle someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: Someone risks death by tangling with a stinging nettle.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something at risk is to imperil it, a synonym.

clue.text: Like some yarn or article almost complete

indicators.note: almost means the article falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
something complete is finished, or ready

explanation.surface: A piece of writing, like a long story, is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a tale, but here it is thread; 'almost' trims THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin, stringy yarn is fibrous and thin, resembling fine strands.

clue.text: Hurried writer left off after time, composed

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after the letter for time

parts.note: someone who hurried ran

indicators.note: left off means the letter for left is dropped from the word for writer

parts.note: a quill is a feather pen, a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A hasty author, leaving after a while, remains calm and collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' is a pen, not an author; 'off' drops L from QUILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A composed person is calm and serene, a synonym.

clue.text: Such epic style in brick interior!

parts.note: someone who is in is at home

indicators.note: the interior of a word is its middle, everything but the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A grand epic style shows up even inside a brick building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but means at home, giving HOME; 'interior' takes RIC from 'brick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad and Odyssey set the pattern for grand epic verse, so the adjective names that style.

clue.text: French pop in to set up volunteers for light work

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another
in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word to is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: pere is French for father, or pop
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A French dad joins a group of volunteers to put on an operatic show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' is slang for father, here in French; 'set up' turns the little word upwards in this down entry before the father goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This form is a short, light opera with spoken dialogue, a lighthearted musical work.

clue.text: Receiver charges printer commission

indicators.note: to charge is to load or fill, so the phrase that follows carries the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Someone receiving charges pays a printer commission.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'printer commission'; 'Receiver' is a telephone-style receiver, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a two-way communication system with speaker and microphone units, so it receives messages within a building.

clue.text: His nebulous list comparatively untidy

definitions.meaning: Charles ..., French astronomer, compiled a catalogue of nebulae and star clusters
the comparative form of a word meaning disorderly

explanation.surface: An astronomer's catalogue of nebulae is rather disorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: A French astronomer catalogued nebulae and clusters, and the comparative of an adjective meaning disordered is spelt identically.

clue.text: Showing individual price of fare in winged chariot

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within another

parts.note: alate is a biological term meaning having wings
a chariot is a kind of car, a wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: Restaurant food is priced separately, served in a winged chariot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winged' gives an unusual biological word meaning having wings, which holds the vehicle; 'fare' is food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu like this prices every dish separately rather than as a set meal.

clue.text: Irishman touring fine Japanese inn

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the man's name goes around the word for fine

parts.note: Ryan is a typical Irish surname or name
OK means fine or satisfactory

explanation.surface: An Irishman on tour finds a fine Japanese inn.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional Japanese guesthouse with tatami floors and communal baths.

clue.text: Fake second rate quartz ultimately this?

definitions.text: Fake second rate quartz ultimately this?

indicators.note: to fake is to falsify or tamper with, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word quartz

explanation.surface: Is this second-rate fake quartz nothing but an imitation?
explanation.walkthrough: S, RATE and Z are rearranged; the whole clue describes a cheap fake stone, and 'Fake' is both the signal and the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation substitute, inferior to the real thing, is exactly what a counterfeit second-rate stone is.

clue.text: Old sovereign, fine Basque one he collected

indicators.note: collected means gathered up and put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A fine Basque person picks up a gold sovereign coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests a gold coin, but it is a ruler; F, BASQUE, ONE and HE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This biblical queen ruled an ancient Arabian kingdom and visited Solomon.

clue.text: Man raised stocks account for everyone

indicators.note: to stock is to hold in store, so the reversed pronoun holds the abbreviation
in a down clue raised means lifted up, read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man raises cattle and keeps the books for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns HE into EH, which 'stocks' AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices given per person, like tickets costing a pound apiece, apply individually to all.

clue.text: Dish that cook regularly presented

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dish that the chef makes regularly is presented.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd letters of 'that cook' give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mexican food is a folded tortilla with a filling, a dish.

clue.text: Rough edge to ring polished off

parts.note: to edge forward is to inch along
O is shaped like a ring
food polished off has been eaten, so it was ate

explanation.surface: The edge of a ring is buffed until rough parts are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polished off' looks like jewellery polishing but means eaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only begun and not yet fully formed is rough and rudimentary.

clue.text: Staff carry outside a sleeping policeman

indicators.note: outside means the word for staff goes around the article

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
to hump something is to carry it laboriously

explanation.surface: Staff carry a dozing police officer outside.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sleeping policeman' is British slang for a speed bump across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names a raised ridge across a road for slowing traffic this way.
